# boot_vm_image

[← Command index](README.md)

Boot an installer image in a throwaway machine, the way the target will.

## Synopsis

```
boot_vm_image [options]
```

## Description

Runs qemu directly with UEFI firmware (OVMF), a blank qcow2 disk and the image in the
drive, so an image from `build_autoinstall_iso` can be watched installing before it
goes anywhere near real hardware. Qemu exits when the installer reboots, which is how
you know it finished: the image is still in the drive, and a machine that carried on
would boot it and start the install over. Run it again without `--iso` to boot what
was installed.

Each machine keeps `<name>.qcow2` and its own copy of the firmware variables,
`<name>-vars.fd`, in `[UserData.VM] vm_dir` (`$HOME/VirtualMachines` by default), so
several images can be tried side by side. Memory, processors, disk size and SSH port
default to `vm_memory`, `vm_vcpus`, `vm_disk_size` and `vm_ssh_port` in the same
section (6144 MB, 4, 60 GB and 2222 when unset). A value given on the command line
wins, including `0`.

Nothing here needs root or libvirt. The machine gets user-mode networking with the
SSH port forwarded, so reach it with `ssh -p 2222 <user>@localhost`.

## Options

### Machine

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-n, --name <name>` | Machine name, which names its disk and its firmware variables. Default: `joybox-boot`. |
| `-i, --iso <iso>` | Image to install from; leave it out to boot what was installed. |
| `-b, --boot_dir <boot_dir>` | Directory for the disk and firmware variables, instead of `[UserData.VM] vm_dir`; created if missing. |
| `-m, --memory <memory>` | Memory in MB; `vm_memory` when omitted. |
| `-c, --vcpus <vcpus>` | Processor count; `vm_vcpus` when omitted. |
| `-z, --disk_size <disk_size>` | Disk size in GB, used only when the disk is created; `vm_disk_size` when omitted. |
| `-t, --ssh_port <ssh_port>` | Local port forwarded to the machine's SSH port; `0` gives the machine no network at all; `vm_ssh_port` when omitted. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-e, --headless` | Open no window, and put the serial console on this terminal. |
| `-l, --serial_file <serial_file>` | With `--headless`, write the serial console to this file instead of the terminal. |
| `-r, --reset` | Delete the machine's disk and firmware variables first and start from nothing. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Install from an image onto a fresh disk

```bash
boot_vm_image -n llm -i ~/Images/llm.iso
```

### Boot what it installed

```bash
boot_vm_image -n llm
```

### Install again from scratch

```bash
boot_vm_image -n llm -i ~/Images/llm.iso -r
```

### Install with no window, console on this terminal

```bash
boot_vm_image -n llm -i ~/Images/llm.iso -e
```

### Install with no window, console to a file

```bash
boot_vm_image -n llm -i ~/Images/llm.iso -e -l ~/llm-console.log
```

### Dry run without creating the disk or starting qemu

```bash
boot_vm_image -n llm -i ~/Images/llm.iso -p -v
```

## Notes

- Needs `qemu-system-x86_64`, `qemu-img` and OVMF firmware (the `ovmf` package) on this machine.
- Without access to `/dev/kvm` the machine still runs, but an install takes hours; the command warns when it starts.
- Installing onto an existing disk without `--reset` installs over it, with a warning.
- `--headless` is only useful with an image built with `--serial_console`; otherwise the terminal shows nothing after the boot menu.
- The server image unpacks into memory, so 4096 MB is tight.
- No GPU is passed through, so driver installs and GPU work are only exercised on real hardware.
